nodes.label: alignment_box
nodes.rationale: Grid-aligned connectors define footprint; highest upward stud sets top; covering studs changes a model's alignment box.

nodes.label: Component factories
nodes.rationale: Size helpers accept only listed argument combinations; rotate a supported size rather than swapping dimensions.

nodes.label: BrickLayer coordinate system (+x left, +y back, +z up; studs/bricks)
nodes.norm_label: bricklayer coordinate system (+x left, +y back, +z up; studs/bricks)
nodes.rationale: One brick = 6/5 stud; PLATE = 1/3 brick; to_stud_units for uniform geometry.

nodes.label: Vec3
nodes.rationale: +/- require same subclass so vectors from different coordinate systems cannot be mixed by accident.

nodes.label: scripts/bw BrickWright wrapper
nodes.rationale: Every BrickWright command goes through scripts/bw because it sets the inventory, required checks and LDraw library; brickwright is never called directly.

nodes.label: lego-builder subagent (Haiku)
nodes.rationale: Cheap Haiku model does the mechanical part placing in build.py; edits only build.py, never adds build steps, never finalizes.

nodes.label: lego-solver subagent (Sonnet)
nodes.rationale: Read-only fixer for one failed check (floating, collisions, connected, inventory); may inspect the build with short Python but does not edit files; keeps plan shape and colors, changes as little as possible.

nodes.label: REBUILD request (SOLVER on/off)
nodes.rationale: Copies an old record's plan.json and expansion.md, skips steps 1-4, one review round with no re-plan, so solver-on and solver-off runs build exactly the same plan for a fair comparison.

nodes.label: Review step (render + checklist pass/fail)
nodes.rationale: Render build.png, judge each checklist item; on failure revise the design (not just details) and rebuild from an empty build.py; max 2 review rounds.

nodes.label: Units: studs (x,y) and bricks (z), 1 brick = 3 plates
nodes.norm_label: units: studs (x,y) and bricks (z), 1 brick = 3 plates

nodes.label: Voxel Build mode (BUILD: requests)
nodes.rationale: Main session acts as planner and reviewer, delegating part placing to lego-builder and hard problems to lego-solver; 8-step flow Questions, Description, Record, Plan, Build, Review, Finish, Report.

nodes.label: API error retry and clean stop (exit 5)
nodes.norm_label: api error retry and clean stop (exit 5)

nodes.label: ask_expert tool (Sonnet edits, Opus rescue)
nodes.rationale: Builder sends only record ID and failed check; code builds a small packet of nearby parts; Sonnet answers structured edits (5 tries per conversation), then Opus (max 3 rescues); cached prompt prefix; saved to expert.json.

nodes.label: Code-computed build steps (pages of 12 parts)
nodes.rationale: Builder does not split steps; code orders parts from the ground up by support, pages of at most 12, writing out/build.ldr and keeping out/build.unordered.ldr.

nodes.label: --from-record plan reuse
nodes.rationale: Compare builder models on the exact same plan by reusing an earlier record's expansion and latest plan.

nodes.label: Inventory check (independent gate)
nodes.rationale: Owned-parts rule is checked inside the agent's tests and again by an independent gate; failed gate reruns the agent with the report (max 2 retries).

nodes.label: Planning call and spare set (plan.json)
nodes.rationale: Builder gets the plan, planned parts and a spare set (max 40 rows, smallest first, plan colors) instead of the full inventory to keep context small.

nodes.label: Opus review call and plan revision (review.json, plans.json)
nodes.norm_label: opus review call and plan revision (review.json, plans.json)

nodes.label: STUCK report protocol
nodes.rationale: If the same check fails twice in a row the builder stops and reports STUCK with check detail, involved code lines and what it tried, so a stronger model can take over instead of looping.

nodes.label: Solver answer format (cause, exact edits, inventory confirmation)
nodes.norm_label: solver answer format (cause, exact edits, inventory confirmation)
nodes.rationale: Answer is one-line cause, copyable build.py edits (e.g. replace line 42 / add bl.Element after line 57), and confirmation the owned inventory covers the edits, so the builder can apply them verbatim.

nodes.label: Build step 5: main session counts failures
nodes.norm_label: build step 5: main session counts failures
nodes.rationale: Builder runs validate at most 2 times and returns the last validate output; main session decides solver vs. retry based on SOLVER setting; cap of 8 builder calls. Note: line 40 lacks a newline so step 6 (Review) is run onto the build_log bullet.

nodes.label: Front is +y orientation rule
nodes.rationale: Front of the model is its largest-y side, the side the front render shows; front features go there.

nodes.label: Owned-parts rule (inventory.json, part AND color)
nodes.rationale: Use only parts in inventory.json matching part and color; ignore inventory.unusable.json.

nodes.label: check_connected(expected_components)
nodes.rationale: expected_components changes only when the request genuinely calls for multiple assemblies.

nodes.label: create_build()
nodes.rationale: Must stay deterministic and free of file writes so checks, previews and exports represent the same build.

nodes.label: tests.check(name, ok, detail)
nodes.rationale: Add measurable request-specific checks; repair the build rather than weakening requirements.

nodes.label: tests.check_motion(samples)
nodes.rationale: Optional; covers sampled poses only, unannotated connections stay rigid which can cause false positives.

nodes.label: Validation harness
nodes.rationale: Harness independently enforces no-floating and no-collision; connectivity and request checks come from run_tests().

nodes.label: Connected (single assembly) requirement
nodes.rationale: Face contact alone does not connect; stagger brick layers or bridge with a shared plate.

nodes.label: Faithful to request requirement
nodes.rationale: Do not remove requested features merely to pass checks.

nodes.label: No floating parts requirement
nodes.rationale: Support via mated connections or surface contact (tiles, ledges, slopes); side contact alone does not count; sliding/tipping unchecked.

nodes.label: Width-first API dimensions
nodes.rationale: LDraw names keep their own dimension order; use spec.shape or measured geometry instead of inferring from names.

nodes.label: BrickWright working method
nodes.rationale: Plan features, look up catalog parts rather than remembered IDs, build incrementally with validation, render to verify visual fidelity, run checks on final source.
